source.title: Unmerge: Efficient Machine Unlearning via Task Arithmetic
source.authors: Hao-Ran Tang; Andrew Tan; Rajiv Khanna

record.file_problem: none; the full paper and appendices are present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports that a linear probe can still recover class information from frozen features after every approximate method it tested, including Unmerge. This qualifies claims that unlearning removes the information, though it does not test the specified recovery attacks directly.
record.gate_note: The paper's standard class-level forget/retain accuracy results and its Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct unlearning comparison do not test recovery by the attacks in the claim. The relevant result is the paper's explicit statement that a linear probe on frozen features still recovers forget classes after every approximate method tested. It does not test small-set relearning, activation-direction ablation, quantization, or prompt attacks. Cited attack results are not included.
record.test_reason: The paper is a vision class-unlearning method study on ResNet-50 and ViT-S/16 with CIFAR-100 and TinyImageNet. Its LLM part (Llama-3.2-3B on TOFU) reports only forget quality and utility, with no recovery attack. The only result bearing on shallowness is a one-sentence, unquantified remark in App. F: a linear probe on frozen features still recovers forget classes after every approximate method. That remark concerns image classifiers, not knowledge in language models, and gives no numbers, model breakdown or protocol. It does not measure what versions A–F name for the same kind of system, so it is recorded under fits_no_version rather than as a test.
record.authors_conclusion: Partly right. The authors' main conclusion is that Unmerge, a training-free low-rank task-vector subtraction, improves the forget/retain tug-of-war over gradient and task-vector baselines on class-level vision unlearning. It also keeps membership-inference exposure near retraining and moves forget features toward the retrained model. In limitations they concede that a linear probe still recovers forget classes from all tested methods, so they claim fidelity to retraining in outputs and feature distribution, not undecodability. The LLM result is preliminary: forget quality 0.131 at utility 0.630 on TOFU, with no robustness testing.
record.recipe_differences: Unmerge is a low-rank, task-vector weight edit for concept-level class unlearning; the paper does not implement the specified relearning, activation-ablation, quantization, or prompting attacks.

fits_no_version.finding: In ResNet-50/ViT image classifiers, a linear probe on frozen features still recovers forget classes after every approximate unlearning method tested, including Unmerge. The remark is qualitative, from App. F.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Class-level approximate unlearning in vision classifiers leaves class information linearly decodable from frozen features.

fits_no_version.finding: Random Label and SalUn reduce forget accuracy but leave forget-class penultimate features cleanly separable from retain. Their relative feature-distance gap to retraining is 1.0–2.5 on CIFAR-100 and about 4 on TinyImageNet (Tab. 3, Tab. 17). A logit mask on the un-edited model already matches retraining on ToW and the MIA gap.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In vision classifiers, relabeling-based unlearning changes outputs while leaving forget representations intact (a label/feature dissociation).

record.code_released: The authors state that code, configurations, and the evaluation pipeline will be released upon acceptance; no URL is stated.
record.problems: The relevant linear-probe finding is qualitative and has no reported probe accuracy, uncertainty, or per-model breakdown. The evidence concerns class information in vision-model features, not targeted factual knowledge in LLMs, and it does not test the recovery attacks named in the claim.
record.rows_left_out: No other results qualify as rows for the tested version: the unlearning accuracy and utility tables do not measure post-unlearning recovery by an attack.

untested.parts: No recovery attack of any kind is run on the unlearned LLM (TOFU) or on the vision models.
No relearning or fine-tuning recovery attack.
No activation-direction ablation, and no LLM analysis of access-blocking versus deletion. There is only an unquantified vision-model probe remark.
No rephrasing, jailbreak, multilingual or in-context attack.
Unmerge is not evaluated against any recovery attack. The authors explicitly disclaim undecodability.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'tests/T5' and its C 'supports' label are rejected. The only shallowness-relevant evidence is an unquantified aside about vision classifiers, a different kind of system from the LLM knowledge unlearning the versions describe. No verdicts are given.

versions.untested_parts: The paper evaluates ordinary unlearning performance but does not test whether simple attacks fail to recover targeted knowledge.
No fine-tuning or relearning attack is evaluated.
No activation-direction ablation is performed. The evidence is a qualitative linear-probe result on frozen features, not a test of every kind of internal edit or access-blocking mechanism.
No weight quantization attack is evaluated.
No prompt rephrasing, jailbreak, language variation, or in-context recovery attack is evaluated.
The paper proposes Unmerge as a class-level unlearning method but does not test whether it resists the attacks in the claim.

rows.subject: every approximate method tested (including U NMERGE)
rows.operation_detail: A linear probe on frozen features is used to test whether forget-class information remains recoverable.
rows.measure: Whether a linear probe recovers forget-class information
rows.value: A linear probe still recovers the forget classes from every approximate method tested, including U NMERGE.
rows.note: Qualitative statement; no probe accuracy or per-model breakdown is given. It indicates that class information remains decodable, but is not an activation-ablation or LLM knowledge-recovery experiment.
rows.check: The subject is vision classifiers (ResNet-50/ViT-S class-level forgetting), not LLM targeted knowledge, so the row does not bear on version C as stated. The value is a qualitative limitations-section remark with no probe accuracy, baseline, models or settings given. The setting is not even stated explicitly, though context implies the vision experiments. It should not support a verdict.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
